Most AI video tools still feel like editors with an AI button bolted on. You type a prompt, receive a rough draft, then spend an hour dragging clips around a timeline. CutBay takes a different approach: you describe what you want, provide source material, and chat with the AI to refine the result.

CutBay.ai Review: Make Videos with an AI Agent by Chatting – iWay Magazine
results.content:
### Worth Keeping in Mind

CutBay is brand new, so independent reviews are still thin on the ground. It makes sense to try it on a real project before building a workflow around it.

As with any AI tool, give the result a once-over before you publish. Check the script, numbers, captions and tone of voice. The canvas editor is there for exactly that.

On pricing, the site invites you to start for free, but the details of the free and paid plans weren’t visible when we looked. Check cutbay.ai/pricing before you commit. The interface is also in English, so if you plan to make videos in other languages, test a short sample first.

### The Verdict [...] ### The Verdict

CutBay’s pitch is refreshingly simple: video should start with an idea, not with software. It takes in the content you already have, builds a full first draft, and lets you refine it by chat or by hand. If you create videos for marketing, teaching or business communication, it’s well worth a spin, and the free start makes that easy.

### FAQ

What is CutBay.ai?  
It’s an AI video agent that turns ideas, documents, links and media files into finished videos, and lets you edit them through chat.

Do I need video editing experience?  
No. You describe what you want and ask for changes in plain language. The canvas editor is there when you want finer control. [...] ### Who Will Get the Most Out of It

 Marketers and ecommerce teams can turn a product URL or landing page into a showcase, promo or launch video.
 Teachers and trainers can turn lessons, tutorials and slides into explainers that are easier to follow.
 Small businesses and consultants can build pitch videos, onboarding materials and animated reports without hiring a motion designer.
 Bloggers and publishers can repurpose written articles as video for YouTube, Shorts and social feeds.

The common thread is people who have good content and a shortage of time or editing skills. For them, CutBay looks like a practical shortcut.
